story.head: Depth vs. Star power
paras: The Islanders (8-6-4) beat Los Angeles 5-2 on Thursday, while the Blue Jackets are on a three-game losing streak. This is a Metropolitan Division matchup, with the Jackets last (29th in the NHL) and the Islanders fifth (tied for 18th).

The Blue Jackets have played better than their record (.412) says: their chances are worth about .486, and their finishing has held them back. The Islanders’ record (.556) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.473), largely thanks to their goaltending.

The Blue Jackets (2nd) and the Islanders (3rd) both get their defensemen shooting. The Blue Jackets get pinned in their own end on long shifts (29th). They also forecheck as hard as almost anyone (3rd), and that could keep the Islanders pinned in their own end. Columbus has scored 2.35 goals a game, the third fewest in the league. On the other side, the Islanders have had the league’s best goaltending (1st). They also roll their lines more evenly than almost anyone (2nd), so the Islanders roll four lines, but the Blue Jackets lean on their top six.

Kent Johnson (8 G / 9 A / 17 P in 17 GP) leads the Blue Jackets in scoring, and Zach Werenski (2 G / 12 A / 14 P in 17 GP) is next in line. Bo Horvat (8 G / 10 A / 18 P in 18 GP) is tied for the Islanders’ scoring lead, with seven goals in eleven games against Columbus since 2023-24. Matthew Schaefer (6 G / 12 A / 18 P in 18 GP) shares it.

Ilya Sorokin (7-4-2 / .915 SV% in 13 GS) has been outstanding for the Islanders and will likely start. Columbus has two options in net: Jet Greaves (2-7-0 / .881 SV% in 9 GS) and Cam Talbot (5-3-0 / .907 SV% in 8 GS). They have split the last ten starts, and Greaves got the last one on Thursday. It’s anyone’s guess who gets the net.
